abstention_policy.selection_rule: Largest swept margin threshold that abstains on at most 15% of VALIDATION rows AND rescues at least 2x as many wrong predictions as the correct ones it costs. Deliberately not a macro-F1 optimization -- abstaining routes rows to 'Other', which dilutes that class's precision, so macro-F1 would select 'never abstain' for the wrong reason. Fitted after the model was frozen, on VALIDATION only; it could not change which model won.

evidence_tier: Sanitized deployment-oriented bank-description benchmark v2 (hand-curated, fabricated merchants; category-typical head nouns shared across many distinct merchant groups so a merchant-group-isolated split still leaves learnable signal -- NOT real-world data)

hypotheses.G10_complement_nb_union: Hypothesis: ComplementNB is specifically designed for imbalanced text classification and is nearly free to fit -- worth one honest attempt.
hypotheses.G11_multinomial_nb_union: Control for G10: the standard Naive Bayes variant, to confirm any NB gain comes from the complement formulation rather than NB in general.
hypotheses.G12_word_unigram_char_union: Hypothesis: word bigrams are near-useless on 2-4 word merchant strings and only dilute the L2 norm; unigrams plus char n-grams may be strictly better.
hypotheses.G13_union_wide_C4: Hypothesis: the wide word+char union is the best representation, and its remaining headroom is regularization -- C=4 on that exact representation.
hypotheses.G14_union_wide_balanced: Hypothesis: on the wide union, class_weight='balanced' trades a little accuracy on the largest category for recall on the smallest ones -- which is what macro-F1 rewards.
hypotheses.G1_mlf_recipe_on_v2: Control: the exact ML-F production recipe (word TF-IDF, 200 features, no normalization) re-fit on the v2 corpus. Isolates how much of the ML-F failure was the corpus rather than the model.
hypotheses.G2_word_unbounded: Hypothesis: the 200-term cap, not the word representation itself, was starving the vocabulary. Remove the cap, change nothing else.
hypotheses.G3_word_unbounded_normalized: Hypothesis: v2 boilerplate stripping (ONLINE PURCHASE / E-TRANSFER / REF-token removal, which ML-F's v1 normalizer missed) frees vocabulary capacity for merchant-identity terms.
hypotheses.G4_char_only: Hypothesis: character n-grams alone survive Scotiabank-style mid-word truncation and the glued ONLINE-PURCHASE-....COM shape, where whole word tokens do not exist.
hypotheses.G5_word_char_union: Hypothesis: word features carry head-noun/merchant identity, char features carry truncation robustness, and a FeatureUnion of both dominates either alone -- the central ML-G representation hypothesis.
hypotheses.G6_word_char_union_wide: Hypothesis: widening the char n-gram range (2-6) and cap catches shorter stems (PHARM, DENT) that 3-5 truncates away.
hypotheses.G7_word_char_union_balanced: Hypothesis: class_weight='balanced' lifts the smaller categories' recall, which is what macro-F1 (as opposed to accuracy) actually rewards.
hypotheses.G8_word_char_union_C4: Hypothesis: with high-dimensional sparse text and few rows per class, the default C=1.0 is over-regularized; C=4 should sharpen the decision boundaries without the vocabulary being large enough to overfit badly.
hypotheses.G9_linear_svm_union: Hypothesis: LinearSVC is the classical strong baseline on sparse text and may beat LogReg on the same representation.

winner_selection_reasoning: Highest VALIDATION macro-F1 among the 14 pre-registered classical candidates, tie-broken within 0.01 toward the simpler representation and then LogReg > LinearSVC > Naive Bayes. Selected before FINAL_TEST was touched. Abstention thresholds were fitted afterwards, on VALIDATION only, and could not change which model won.
